name: Nobu Hotel Marbella
positioning: Nobu hotel within the Puente Romano resort on Marbella's Golden Mile, steps from the Mediterranean beaches, pairing Andalusian charm with Nobu's Japanese aesthetic
best_for: Couples who want a beach stay with a Six Senses spa, an adults-only pool and Nobu dining
Tennis players who want clay, plexipave and padel courts with pro coaching
Families who want a kids club with daily activities

facts.text: The hotel sits on Marbella's Golden Mile in Southern Spain, steps from the sandy beaches of the Mediterranean.
The hotel is part of the Puente Romano resort.
The hotel pairs Andalusian charm with Nobu's signature Japanese aesthetic.
Rooms have brown marble bathrooms, minimal lines and lots of wood, with linen furnishings.
Rooms come with Japanese yukata robes.
The spa's hammam has herbal and regular steam rooms, a sauna, hot-and-cold therapy showers and various hydrotherapy pools.
The fitness facility has Technogym equipment and a private studio for spin, barre and boxing classes.
The hotel offers daily complimentary classes, including yoga and Pilates.
Nobu Marbella serves signature dishes, including Black Cod Miso and Yellowtail Sashimi, at a sushi bar, in the dining room or on a terrace overlooking La Plaza.
Guests have access to La Plaza, a fine dining and nightlife scene set along the Mediterranean.
Service follows Omotenashi, the Japanese spirit of hospitality.

highlights.text: Six Senses Spa offers treatments in traditional treatment rooms, canopied cabana rooms, or by the sea.
Nobu Pool is an adults-only pool reserved for hotel guests.
The resort's tennis club has 8 clay courts, 2 plexipave courts and 4 padel courts, with coaching sessions with a pro and matches with other guests.
Balconies look over the resort's rooftops or, in some rooms, across the sea.
La Casita Kids Club runs a daily activities program, including tennis coaching, art masterclasses and cooking lessons, including Nobu sushi workshops.

considerations.text: There are some ramps throughout the resort, but many rooms are reached by stairs alone.
Conde Nast Traveler advises booking spa treatments in advance.
WhataHotel notes limited availability during the peak summer season.
